label: Sequence start (t=0, specific first-token set) plus second copy output when L=3
explanation: Two deterministic, position-locked conditions. (1) At t=0 it fires every time the first input is one of b c d e f g l m q s t u x y z 0 1 2, and never when it is a h i j k n o p r v w 3. This accounts for about 96% of activations but only about 80% of mass, because these activations are small (about 0.02-0.19 of max). (2) In length-3 sequences it fires at t=4, the step right after the first copy output, where the input is orig(0) and the output is orig(1). It fires there for every first token, including tokens outside the t=0 set, and these are the strongest activations (up to max; about 20% of mass). Activation magnitude depends mostly on which of the two conditions holds, then on the token. It never fires at t=1..3, at the delimiter, or at any copy step other than t=4 with L=3, and it does not depend on whether the copy is correct.

issues: No refutation found. Test split scores are P=R=F1=mass recall=1.0, and misses --split test shows 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

The profile matches every factual claim. The unit never fires at t=1..3, at the delimiter, or at copy steps other than t=4. t=0 holds about 80% of activation mass and t=4 about 20%. At t=4 it fires in all L=3 sequences (2605/2605 on dev), and that includes first tokens outside the t=0 set (a, k, n, o, p, h appear among the top examples). Activations at t=0 run about 0.02-0.19 of max, while t=4 reaches the max. Correctness has no effect.
Minor: the label does not mention that the t=0 component accounts for most of the mass, but the explanation states it. The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
